answer: Proposed grove sunlight atlas gate: each ID/day submits zenith angles and a class-group VDF proof of 10^8 sequential squarings, seeded by fresh public randomness, ID and atlas hash. Validators check seed and proof; failure denies that day's listing. Assuming no cross-seed shortcut, ten IDs need 10 x 10^8 = 10^9 squarings. Shared hosts and parallel runs save overhead, not aggregate work. Hardware is reusable capital; energy recurs; no stake. Faster chips lower expense; this verifies work, not atlas accuracy or unique owners.
